studies.title: What They Sent And What They Left
studies.meaning: Two things are written down and the second is the unexpected one. What people sent ahead, meaning their own acts, and their traces: what carried on after them and because of them. The commentators read the traces broadly, as the footprints left walking toward something good and as the consequences that outlive a person, and they hold both together. The word for the register is unusual, since it ordinarily means a leader or something followed, so the record is named as a thing that goes in front rather than behind.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The surah has just described people so closed that warning makes no difference to them, and then turns to say who can be reached. This ayah interrupts with a statement about what is being recorded, and the next line moves straight into a story about a town that received messengers. The record and the parable are set side by side deliberately rather than by accident of sequence.

keyTerms.note: The verb for sending goods ahead of yourself on a journey. Deeds are pictured as consignments dispatched to a destination the sender has not reached yet, waiting there on arrival.
Marks left behind by something that has passed, from footprints in sand to the ruins of a camp. Recording them means a person is accounted for by effects as well as by acts.
The ordinary sense is a leader or a guide walked behind. Used of the record, it makes the tally something that goes in front, which is why translations differ over how to render it here.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Tracking was a real profession. A man who knew the ground could read from prints in sand how many had passed, how heavily their animals were loaded, and roughly when, and trackers were hired to follow raiders across country. Footprints were treated as evidence in disputes. An audience that took tracks seriously as testimony would hear a record including traces as a natural extension.
studies.didYouKnow: The classical sources preserve a report connected with this ayah, in which a clan living at a distance from the mosque considered moving closer to it and were told that their footsteps on the way were being written down. The report is cited by the commentators precisely because the ayah names traces alongside deeds.
studies.theologicalSignificance: What is recorded exceeds what was performed. Including traces means a person is accounted for by effects they did not carry out and may never have learned about, which widens responsibility in both directions: unintended good is counted, and so is damage set in motion and left running. Naming the register as something that leads rather than follows suggests it is not only a report compiled afterwards.

crossReferences.why: Puts the same pairing as an announcement: informed of what he sent forward and what he left behind.
Describes the record from the other side, leaving out nothing small and nothing large.
Reduces the scale to its limit, an atom's weight of good or of evil brought into view.

studies.applyIt: Name one thing you started that is still running without you: a habit somebody copied, a group that still meets, a phrase your children use. Ask whether you would want it in the column this ayah describes. If not, you can usually still reach it. Traces are the part of a life that stays editable longest.

studies.title: All The Pairs He Made
studies.meaning: A single sentence of praise built on one word: pairs. Three domains are named and the third is where the sentence does its work. What the earth sends up, what human beings are themselves, and then what they do not know. The commentators take the pairs as the matched kinds running through creation, and they notice that the ayah refuses to close its own list. It ends by naming a category whose contents are unavailable, which leaves the praise open rather than complete.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The ayah sits inside the surah's run of signs, between ground brought back to life so that people can eat from it and the night stripped away from the day. It is the only place in that sequence where the argument pauses for a formula of glorification instead of continuing to describe. The surrounding ayat end by asking whether people will be thankful.

keyTerms.gloss: glory be to, far removed is
keyTerms.note: From a root meaning to swim or move freely away. The formula declares distance from any deficiency rather than describing a quality, which is why it functions as a refusal more than a description.
One word covering a couple, a species and one of two matched things. It is also the ordinary word for a spouse, which is why translations of this ayah divide between pairs and kinds.
The verb for a plant being brought up out of soil, with the earth as its subject. Naming the ground as the one doing the producing keeps the sign inside something the listener has watched.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Pairing was work, not a fact people had read about. Date palms carry male and female flowers on separate trees, so growers in Arabia climbed and pollinated by hand every season, and a plantation left to itself produced almost nothing. Breeding stock was selected and remembered by line. An audience that pollinated trees each spring knew pairing as a thing they were responsible for.
studies.didYouKnow: The word translated here as pairs is the same word the Quran uses for a husband or a wife. Arabic makes no separation between a spouse, a species and one half of a matched set, which is why translators of this single ayah divide between rendering it as pairs, as kinds, and as mates, all defensibly.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah closes an argument by leaving it open. Two known domains are named and a third is deliberately left blank, so what is being praised explicitly includes what the one praising cannot list. That makes the formula structurally honest. It declares distance rather than claiming a description, and it leaves room for whatever is discovered later without having laid claim to it in advance.

crossReferences.why: States the principle plainly: of everything two matched kinds were made, so that people might remember.
Applies the same pairing to fruits, alongside the rivers, the mountains and the covering of night.
Narrows the word to its most familiar sense, the two mates, male and female, from a single drop.

studies.applyIt: Name one thing you learned this year that you did not previously know existed: a creature, a mechanism, a word for something you had felt but never labelled. Let it stand as the third clause of this ayah for a moment. The sentence was built with a space in it, and the space is where anything you find later belongs.

studies.title: Each Floats In Its Course
studies.meaning: Two impossibilities are stated as proprieties rather than as physics. The sun is not to catch the moon; the night is not to outrun the day. The verb means that a thing is not fitting, so regularity is presented as restraint kept rather than as a constraint imposed. Then the passage moves without transition from courses in the sky to a loaded ship, and the Arabic makes the join audible: the word for the orbit and the word for the vessel are written with the same letters.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The surah's run of signs has moved through dead ground revived, the night, the sun running to its appointed place, and the moon in its phases. Here it arrives at ships, first the ark that carried ancestors and then the ordinary vessels people ride now. Mecca's trade reached the Red Sea ports, so the second half brought the argument from the beginning of human history to a harbour the audience knew.

keyTerms.note: A verb of propriety rather than of capacity. It says the thing would be out of place, not that it is impossible, which describes the order of the sky as conduct held to rather than force applied.
From a root meaning roundness, used of a spindle whorl and of anything circling. The same three letters, differently vowelled, give the word for a ship in the very next ayah.
A passive form meaning packed to capacity. It is the word for a vessel carrying as much as it safely can, which places the whole image at the edge of what stays afloat.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Red Sea shipping brought grain from Egypt and goods from Abyssinia to the Arabian coast, and Meccan merchants dealt in what came off those boats. Vessels were loaded to the limit because the voyage itself was the expensive part and space was the thing being sold. Everyone had seen an overladen ship low in the water, and everybody knew what occasionally happened to one.
studies.didYouKnow: The Arabic word for the orbit in the first of these ayat and the Arabic word for the ship in the second are written with exactly the same three letters and differ only in their vowels. Two consecutive ayat therefore turn on one word carried from the sky down to the sea, which the recitation makes audible and translation cannot.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Order is described in terms of restraint rather than of force, and that changes what regularity means: the sun does not overtake because it is not for it to, not because it lacks the capacity. The passage then carries the same idea into human history. A loaded ship stays up under conditions the surah says a few lines later could be withdrawn, so what looks like a property of the vessel is treated as a permission granted.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same image and the same verb of swimming, with each body running in a course of its own.
Describes ships raised in the sea like landmarks, listed among the favours being counted out.
Completes the thought two ayat later: drowning is withheld only as a mercy and for a time.

studies.applyIt: On your next journey, by any means, name one part of the machinery you are trusting completely and have never inspected: a bolt, a brake line, a section of track. Nothing to fix, just notice it once. The passage puts the ark and the bus in the same sentence, and both stay up on terms nobody riding them arranged.

studies.title: Peace A Word From A Lord
studies.meaning: Five short ayat move through three registers. Abundance is described by leaving its contents open: whatever they call for. Then a single word of greeting with its source attached, peace spoken from a Merciful Lord, which the commentators treat as higher than everything listed before it. Then a sudden order to stand apart, and a question about an agreement made long ago. Serving is presented as unavoidable in one direction or another; what the covenant settles is not whether but whom.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The surah has been working through the argument with those who rejected the message, and here it sets out the two outcomes side by side. The address at the covenant is not to a tribe or a generation but to the children of Adam, which lifts the question above the particular people being argued with. The commentators connect it to the acknowledgement described elsewhere as taken at the beginning.

keyTerms.note: The verb for calling out and for laying claim to something. Leaving the object unstated is what makes the promise open, since the contents are supplied by whoever is asking.
A verb of sorting, used of distinguishing one thing from a mixture. What it describes is a division of people who had until then been standing together, which is the sentence before any sentence.
From the root of an agreement kept in view and returned to. Framing the question this way makes the exchange a dispute over an existing contract rather than an accusation from nowhere.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Agreements were oral, formal and public, made before witnesses who carried them in memory for decades. Opening a dispute with the question whether an agreement had been made was a recognised move, and everyone present would expect the terms to be recited next. Being told to stand apart from a gathering was itself a public verdict, delivered before any penalty was named.
studies.didYouKnow: The form of address used here, children of Adam, appears in only five places in the whole Quran. Four of them are in Surah 7, clustered within a few ayat of each other, and this is the fifth and last. The phrase that sounds like a standard way of addressing humanity is in fact reserved for a handful of moments.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The covenant language reframes the choice being offered. It is not put as a choice between serving and not serving, but between two objects of service, one of which has already been described as an open enemy. The greeting does something similar in the other direction. What the Garden finally amounts to is stated as a word spoken by God, so the reward is described as being addressed rather than as contents received.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same address to warn the children of Adam against the one who stripped their parents.
Gives the same single word as the greeting exchanged there, with praise opening and closing it.
Describes the acknowledgement taken at the beginning that this question about a covenant recalls.

studies.applyIt: Notice one thing today that you obey without ever having decided to: a notification you answer mid-sentence, a craving you act on before you have registered it, a schedule nobody imposed. Name it out loud once. The passage says service is happening either way, and the first step is finding out what is currently receiving yours.

studies.title: Be And It Comes To Be
studies.meaning: The sentence answers a question raised a few ayat earlier about who could revive bones that have crumbled. It answers by removing the assumption inside the question, which was that difficulty rises with size. Command is described as speech with nothing at all between the saying and the happening. Commentators are careful about the word for command here: it does not describe a syllable God requires, but puts effective will into language a listener can follow. The second ayah turns from mechanism to praise.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, and these are the closing lines of the surah. The ayat before them report someone crumbling an old bone and asking who could bring it back. The answer works backwards through the first origination, then fire drawn out of green wood, then the making of the heavens, and arrives here. The commentators report an occasion involving a Meccan objector with a decayed bone, though their accounts name different men.

keyTerms.note: One word covering an order given and a matter being handled. The Quran uses it for both, so the sentence describes a decision and its execution without a gap between them.
The shortest possible imperative in Arabic, two letters. Its brevity is part of the argument, since the whole distance between intention and existence is expressed in the smallest available word.
An intensive form of the ordinary word for kingdom, occurring only four times in the Quran. It names sovereignty as a realm rather than as an authority exercised over one.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A chief's word was the machinery of that world. An order spoken in the assembly moved men, animals and goods, and its force was measured precisely by how little distance lay between the saying and the doing. A man whose instructions needed repeating or enforcing was known to be weak. Everyone listening could rank authority on that scale, so a word requiring nothing after it described the top of it.
studies.didYouKnow: The word for dominion in the final ayah is an intensified form of the ordinary word for a kingdom, and it appears only four times in the entire Quran. Twice it is what Abraham is shown of the heavens and the earth, once it is offered as a question to those who reject the message, and once it closes this surah.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Power and effort are separated completely. Creation is described without any process at all, which is a claim about what kind of thing God is rather than about how quickly an event happens. Then the surah declines to leave the argument standing as a proof. It closes with glorification and with a direction of travel instead, so the demonstration ends by turning the reader rather than by settling a dispute.

crossReferences.why: States the same formula in a different setting, applied to the originating of the heavens and the earth.
Adds the element of time, describing the single command as no slower than the blink of an eye.
Uses the same rare word for dominion, describing what Abraham was shown of the heavens and the earth.

studies.applyIt: Think of one thing you have privately filed as impossible: a person who will not change, a situation with no exit. You do not have to talk yourself out of the judgement. Just identify the assumption you are leaning on, which is usually that size and difficulty run together. This ayah takes that assumption apart and offers nothing else.
